from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    # Grid separators are the rows and columns with the strongest repeated color.
    row_scores = [max(Counter(row).values()) / w for row in grid]
    col_scores = [
        max(Counter(grid[r][c] for r in range(h)).values()) / h
        for c in range(w)
    ]
    sep_rows = [r for r, s in enumerate(row_scores) if s >= 0.70]
    sep_cols = [c for c, s in enumerate(col_scores) if s >= 0.70]

    # The separator color is the most common value at separator intersections.
    crossings = [grid[r][c] for r in sep_rows for c in sep_cols]
    line_color = Counter(crossings).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Keep just the rectangle containing the colored marks.
    marked = [(i, j) for i, r in enumerate(sep_rows)
              for j, c in enumerate(sep_cols)
              if grid[r][c] != line_color]
    r0 = min(i for i, _ in marked)
    r1 = max(i for i, _ in marked)
    c0 = min(j for _, j in marked)
    c1 = max(j for _, j in marked)
    matrix = [[grid[sep_rows[i]][sep_cols[j]] for j in range(c0, c1 + 1)]
              for i in range(r0, r1 + 1)]

    background = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row
                         if v != line_color).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out = []
    for r in range(len(matrix) - 1):
        row = []
        for c in range(len(matrix[0]) - 1):
            block = [matrix[r][c], matrix[r][c + 1],
                     matrix[r + 1][c], matrix[r + 1][c + 1]]
            row.append(block[0] if all(v == block[0] for v in block)
                       else background)
        out.append(row)
    return out
